artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: extract(bronze_uri, body, ext): one JSON-serialisable document per bronze object, naming bronze_key/bronze_sha256/method_version/type/extractable(/reason). DOCX via zipfile+lxml over word/document.xml + word/styles.xml (paragraphs with resolved style name + bold flag; headings by Heading*/Title style OR an all-bold <=8-word paragraph; tables as rows of cell text). PDF via PyMuPDF get_text('dict') (pages; headings by per-page median-size ratio 1.15x or bold, <=8 words; NEVER find_tables()). XLSX via openpyxl read_only, loaded twice (values, formulas); vendor cache sheets (_CIQHiddenCacheSheet, __FDSCACHE__) never indexed into the workbook at all; mnemonics/factset_codes/calls_seen from quoted upper-case tokens inside formula calls, reading BOTH plain-str formulas and ArrayFormula-typed cells (a real corpus shape -- see the artifact_covered_by AC2 evidence and surprise row AMGT_CORPUS-Z-W1-S1). --write measured live against the 123 bronze research-report objects: objects 123 extracted 120 not_extracted 3 crash 0 stored 123. --census measured live: bronze_objects 123 extractions 123 missing 0; k3 pdf 52 text_extractable 52 zero_text 0 median_chars 15642 skeleton_heading_hits 33 of 52; k4 xlsx 43 opened 43 failed 0 with_mnemonics 37 factset_coded 0.

4 tests under the package poison, each building its own fixture in code (zipfile for DOCX, PyMuPDF for PDF, openpyxl for XLSX) -- no boto3/network call anywhere, extract() takes bytes directly: (1) DOCX headings found both routes -- a Heading1-style paragraph and a separate bold short paragraph both land in headings, a long plain paragraph does not; (2) PDF heading found by size (24pt vs 10pt body, page median ratio) and the long body line is excluded (negative arm); (3) XLSX: PX_LAST found in mnemonics (from a real =BDP(...) quoted arg), FF_SALES lands in factset_codes (from a real =FDS(...) quoted arg), and __FDSCACHE__ is listed in `sheets` but has no `sheet_data` entry and its cell text is absent from the whole serialised document (proving it was never opened); (4) PNG gives extractable False with reason 'not-extracted: png'.

Answers K3 (yes -- 52 of 52 PDF-only reports produced extractable text, 33 of 52 surfaced a skeleton-name heading) and the first half of K4 (yes -- 43 of 43 workbooks opened without Excel; 37 of 43 carry real quoted-token mnemonics; factset_coded reads 0 of 43 under the ruled literal-quoted-token method because the corpus's FactSet-coded variant references its mnemonic by CELL REFERENCE rather than a literal quoted string -- documented with direct cell-level evidence and handed off via AMGT_CORPUS-Z-W1-S1) with the printed --census lines quoted verbatim as evidence, and names what it could not measure (why 19 of 52 PDFs show no skeleton heading; whether cell-reference resolution would raise the FactSet count).

Row AMGT_CORPUS-Z-W1-S1 appended (append-only channel, validated by .tools/surprise-row-gate.py: 1 new row of 4 total checked, all step-7/step-10 fields present) recording the cell-reference-vs-literal-quoted-token gap and the ArrayFormula bug this worker caught and fixed in the same pass before the wrong extraction objects were left standing.

declared_exclusions.item: Typing found mnemonics onto standard Bloomberg mnemonics, or resolving a cell-referenced FactSet mnemonic to its label text
declared_exclusions.reason: Section 1: 'Typing the typing onto mnemonics is CRPS-c-9's.' This cell only finds and reports quoted tokens inside formula calls, exactly as ruled; it does not resolve a cell reference to the label text it points at (that would be a different, larger extraction task -- named in the K3/K4 card and surprise row AMGT_CORPUS-Z-W1-S1, not attempted here).

declared_exclusions.item: OCR of any PDF or any classification/period/typing work on extracted documents
declared_exclusions.reason: Section 1 'What this cell does NOT do': 'no typing, classing or period work (that is CRPS-c-3), no OCR, no library read, no Claude call.' Every PDF in this population already carries a text layer (zero_text 0 of 52), so OCR absence does not affect K3's answer.

declared_exclusions.item: Any read of the OneDrive research library, or any vendor/Claude API call
declared_exclusions.reason: BOUNDS: 'THIS CELL NEVER TOUCHES THE LIBRARY: it reads bronze from the store' and 'NEVER CALL A VENDOR API OR THE CLAUDE API.' extract.py's only imports beyond stdlib/lxml/fitz/openpyxl are lib.research.harvest.store (used only in the CLI's --write/--census, both S3-only); no library.py/backlog.py import exists in this module. test_extract.py never calls _run_write/_run_census, so it never touches boto3 either -- proven by all 4 tests passing under the package poison (which raises on boto3.client/resource/Session.client/subprocess.run/Popen/socket.create_connection).

declared_exclusions.item: Using PyMuPDF's find_tables() for PDF heading detection
declared_exclusions.reason: BOUNDS, ISSUER NOTES: 'the find_tables prohibition is an estate lesson (PyMuPDF reports a wrapped Word heading as a 2x2 table).' _extract_pdf never calls find_tables(); PDF headings come only from get_text('dict') span size/bold heuristics.

declared_exclusions.item: Opening or reading any cell of a sheet named _CIQHiddenCacheSheet or __FDSCACHE__
declared_exclusions.reason: Section 1: 'Per sheet NOT named _CIQHiddenCacheSheet or __FDSCACHE__, emit labels ... and mnemonics.' _extract_xlsx skips these two sheet names BEFORE ever indexing into the workbook object for them (values_wb[name]/formulas_wb[name] are never called) -- proven offline by test_xlsx_mnemonic_and_factset_code_and_cache_sheet_not_opened, which asserts the cache sheet's own cell text is absent from the ENTIRE serialised document, not merely from its own sheet_data entry.
